evidence_items.locator: Key Survey Findings; About the Survey

receipt.public_excerpt: Only 2% say they generally don’t need to revise what AI produces.

evidence_items.explanation: The survey of 1,100 US AI users at larger employers also reports weekly cleanup and negative consequences from low-quality outputs. Together these support recurring workslop, although revision alone does not necessarily indicate poor quality.

receipt.public_excerpt: Just 69% say AI helps, compared to 94% of trained workers.

evidence_items.explanation: Reported benefits remain common even alongside cleanup, and training is associated with different experiences. This limits any inference that recurring workslop makes AI generally unhelpful.

evidence_items.locator: The Hidden Cost to Workers; Methodology

receipt.public_excerpt: Two-thirds of workers report spending up to six or more hours each week correcting AI-related errors.

evidence_items.explanation: This release describes recurring correction work among respondents already screened for encountering workslop. Its methodology explicitly dates fieldwork to January 8, 2025, so it is neither current-period evidence nor an estimate of prevalence among all workers.

unresolved_gaps: No representative denominator for all LLM-generated workplace outputs was established.
The principal evidence is unweighted, sponsor-funded self-report from US AI users at employers with at least 250 employees.
The studies do not separate model limitations from poor prompting, missing context or inadequate human review.
The Zety release's stated 2025 field date was not silently corrected to 2026.
